people.name: Naguib Mahfouz
people.why: The first Arabic-language writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

people.name: Umm Kulthum
people.why: The Arab world stopped for her monthly radio concerts; four million attended her funeral.

people.name: Cleopatra VII
people.why: The last ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, and a formidable politician rather than merely a romantic figure.

people.name: Taha Hussein
people.why: Blind from childhood, he became the dean of Arabic letters and made education free.

people.name: Ahmed Zewail
people.why: Won the Nobel Prize for femtochemistry, watching chemical bonds break in real time.

events.title: The Great Pyramid
events.what: The tallest building on earth for nearly 4,000 years, and the only surviving ancient wonder.

events.title: Tutankhamun's tomb
events.what: Howard Carter's find, largely intact, made ancient Egypt a global obsession.

events.title: The Suez Crisis
events.what: Nasser nationalised the canal; the failed British-French-Israeli response marked the end of an era.

events.title: The revolution
events.what: Eighteen days in Tahrir Square ended Mubarak's thirty-year rule.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Koshari — rice, lentils, pasta and fried onion — is the national street dish; ful medames for breakfast.

culture.label: Humour
culture.text: Egyptians are known across the Arab world for jokes, especially about their own government.

culture.label: Cinema
culture.text: Cairo was the Hollywood of the Arab world, and Egyptian Arabic is understood everywhere because of it.

culture.label: Ahwa
culture.text: Coffee houses where men play backgammon and smoke shisha for hours.

culture.label: Coexistence
culture.text: A large Coptic Christian minority whose church dates to the first century.

talkAbout: Food, and where to get the best koshari.
Ancient history — but Egyptians live in a modern country too.
Football, especially Al Ahly versus Zamalek.
avoid: Politics and the military are risky topics. Don't treat modern Egypt as a museum attached to the pyramids.

people.name: Chinua Achebe
people.why: Things Fall Apart is the most widely read African novel ever written.

people.name: Wole Soyinka
people.why: The first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 1986.

people.name: Fela Kuti
people.why: Invented Afrobeat and used it to attack successive military governments.

people.name: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
people.why: Half of a Yellow Sun and her talk on the danger of a single story reached readers everywhere.

people.name: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
people.why: The first woman and first African to lead the World Trade Organization.

events.title: Nok and Ife
events.what: Terracotta and later bronze sculpture of extraordinary sophistication, centuries before European contact.

events.title: The Benin Expedition
events.what: British forces sacked Benin City and looted thousands of bronzes now in museums worldwide.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Nigeria left British rule as Africa's most populous country.

events.title: The Biafran War
events.what: A secession attempt and the famine that followed killed perhaps a million people.

culture.label: Afrobeats
culture.text: Nigerian pop is the dominant sound of African music worldwide, and increasingly of global charts.

culture.label: Nollywood
culture.text: One of the largest film industries on earth by volume, watched across the continent.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Jollof rice — and the argument with Ghana over who does it better is entirely serious.

culture.label: Diversity
culture.text: Over 500 languages; Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo are the largest, with Nigerian Pidgin as a bridge.

culture.label: Respect
culture.text: Greetings are elaborate and unhurried; in Yoruba culture, younger people may kneel or prostrate.

talkAbout: Music — everyone has opinions on the current artists.
Jollof rice, with the understanding that Nigeria wins.
avoid: Scam-email jokes are tiresome and insulting. Biafra, religion and regional politics are all sensitive.

people.name: Nelson Mandela
people.why: Twenty-seven years in prison, then led the country out of apartheid without a war.

people.name: Desmond Tutu
people.why: Nobel laureate who coined 'Rainbow Nation' and chaired the Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

people.name: Miriam Makeba
people.why: Mama Africa, exiled for thirty years for speaking against apartheid at the UN.

people.name: Christiaan Barnard
people.why: Performed the world's first human heart transplant in Cape Town in 1967.

people.name: Nadine Gordimer
people.why: Nobel laureate whose novels dissected apartheid from the inside, several of them banned.

events.title: Apartheid begins
events.what: The National Party made racial segregation the legal foundation of the state.

events.title: The Soweto uprising
events.what: Schoolchildren protesting compulsory Afrikaans were shot; the images changed world opinion.

events.title: The first free election
events.what: Queues stretched for miles; Mandela became president.

events.title: The Rugby World Cup
events.what: Mandela in a Springbok jersey handing over the trophy became the image of a country trying to hold together.

culture.label: Braai
culture.text: The barbecue is a national institution with its own public holiday on 24 September.

culture.label: Eleven languages
culture.text: Twelve official languages including sign language; most South Africans speak several.

culture.label: Sport
culture.text: Rugby, cricket and football, each with its own history in the country's divisions.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: From isicathamiya and kwaito to amapiano, which has gone global.

culture.label: Ubuntu
culture.text: 'A person is a person through other people' — a philosophy invoked seriously in public life.

talkAbout: Braai, and how to do it properly.
avoid: Race, land reform, crime and inequality are all live and painful. Don't treat 1994 as having solved everything.

people.name: Wangari Maathai
people.why: Founded the Green Belt Movement and became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

people.name: Jomo Kenyatta
people.why: Led Kenya to independence and became its first president.

people.name: Eliud Kipchoge
people.why: The first person to run a marathon in under two hours, and double Olympic champion.

people.name: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
people.why: Abandoned English for Gikuyu and argued that language is where colonisation lives longest.

people.name: Lupita Nyong'o
people.why: Won an Academy Award for 12 Years a Slave and became a global figure.

events.title: The Mau Mau uprising
events.what: A rebellion against British rule met with mass detention and torture; Britain apologised in 2013.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Kenya left British rule; Jamhuri Day on 12 December marks it.

events.title: M-Pesa launches
events.what: Mobile money transformed banking in Kenya and became a model copied worldwide.

events.title: The new constitution
events.what: Devolved power to 47 counties and strengthened the bill of rights after post-election violence.

culture.label: Running
culture.text: The Rift Valley highlands have produced more world-class distance runners than anywhere else.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Ugali with sukuma wiki, nyama choma grilled meat, and chai boiled with milk.

culture.label: Harambee
culture.text: 'Pulling together' — community fundraising for school fees, hospital bills and building projects.

culture.label: M-Pesa
culture.text: Most Kenyans pay by phone; the country leapfrogged card payments entirely.

culture.label: Wildlife
culture.text: The Maasai Mara wildebeest migration is among the greatest natural spectacles on earth.

talkAbout: Running, and which county the champions come from.
avoid: Ethnic politics and election violence are sensitive. Don't treat Kenya as only a safari destination, and don't reduce Maasai culture to a photo opportunity.

people.name: Haile Selassie
people.why: Ruled for 44 years, appealed to the League of Nations against Italian invasion, and is revered by Rastafari.

people.name: Abebe Bikila
people.why: Won Olympic gold in Rome running barefoot, the first Black African Olympic champion.

people.name: Tirunesh Dibaba
people.why: Three Olympic golds and one of the greatest distance runners in history.

people.name: Menelik II
people.why: Defeated Italy at Adwa and kept Ethiopia independent through the scramble for Africa.

people.name: Aster Aweke
people.why: One of Ethiopia's most celebrated voices, known across the diaspora.

events.title: The Kingdom of Aksum
events.what: A trading empire with its own script and coinage, and one of the first states to adopt Christianity.

events.title: Lalibela
events.what: Eleven churches carved downward out of solid rock, still in use today.

events.title: The Battle of Adwa
events.what: Ethiopia crushed an Italian invasion — the only African state to defeat a European coloniser and stay independent.

events.title: The Derg
events.what: A military junta deposed Haile Selassie and ruled through famine and terror until 1991.

culture.label: Coffee
culture.text: Coffee originated here, and the ceremony — roasting, grinding and three rounds — can take hours.

culture.label: Injera
culture.text: Sour teff flatbread that serves as plate, cutlery and food, shared from one platter.

culture.label: Calendar
culture.text: Ethiopia runs seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar, with thirteen months.

culture.label: Orthodoxy
culture.text: One of the world's oldest churches, with its own canon, fasting rules and Ge'ez liturgy.

culture.label: Script
culture.text: Amharic uses Ge'ez script, one of the few writing systems developed in Africa and still in daily use.

talkAbout: Never having been colonised, and Adwa.
avoid: Tigray, Amhara and Oromo politics are acutely sensitive and currently violent. The 1984 famine is not the whole of the country.

people.name: Ibn Battuta
people.why: Travelled around 120,000 km across Africa, Asia and Europe — further than anyone before modern times.

people.name: Fatima al-Fihri
people.why: Founded al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, recognised as the oldest continuously operating university in the world.

people.name: Hicham El Guerrouj
people.why: Holds the mile and 1500 m world records, both standing for over twenty years.

people.name: Tahar Ben Jelloun
people.why: Won the Prix Goncourt and writes on Moroccan life and migration in French.

people.name: Leila Slimani
people.why: Another Goncourt winner, and among the most read Francophone writers today.

events.title: The Idrisid dynasty
events.what: The first Moroccan Muslim state, founded at Fez.

events.title: Marrakesh founded
events.what: The Almoravid capital gave the country its European name.

events.title: The French protectorate
events.what: Four decades of French and Spanish control, ending with independence under Mohammed V.

events.title: World Cup semi-final
events.what: Morocco became the first African and Arab team to reach a World Cup semi-final.

culture.label: Mint tea
culture.text: Poured from a height to aerate it, offered constantly, and refusing is nearly impossible.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Tagine, couscous on Fridays, and pastilla — a pigeon pie dusted with cinnamon and sugar.

culture.label: Languages
culture.text: Darija Arabic and Amazigh are both official, with French widely used in business.

culture.label: Medinas
culture.text: Fez el Bali is one of the largest car-free urban areas in the world.

culture.label: Gnawa
culture.text: Music with sub-Saharan roots, played on the guembri in all-night trance ceremonies.

talkAbout: The Atlas mountains and the desert.
avoid: Western Sahara and the monarchy are not open subjects. Bargaining is expected, but haggling aggressively over small sums reads poorly.

people.name: Kwame Nkrumah
people.why: Led the first sub-Saharan colony to independence and was the great voice of Pan-Africanism.

people.name: Kofi Annan
people.why: Led the UN for a decade and shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 2001.

people.name: Yaa Asantewaa
people.why: Led the Ashanti war against the British in 1900 when the men hesitated.

people.name: Ama Ata Aidoo
people.why: A founding figure of African women's writing in English, and a former education minister.

people.name: Abedi Pele
people.why: Three-time African Footballer of the Year and a European Cup winner with Marseille.

events.title: The Ashanti Empire
events.what: A powerful state built on gold, with the Golden Stool as the soul of the nation.

events.title: The slave forts
events.what: Elmina and Cape Coast castles were among the largest slave-trading posts on the coast.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule.

events.title: The Year of Return
events.what: Ghana invited the African diaspora home on the 400th anniversary of the first enslaved arrivals in Virginia.

culture.label: Kente
culture.text: Handwoven Ashanti cloth where every pattern and colour carries a specific meaning.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Jollof rice, waakye, banku and fufu with light soup — and the jollof argument with Nigeria.

culture.label: Fantasy coffins
culture.text: Ga carpenters build coffins shaped like fish, aeroplanes or cocoa pods to suit the life lived.

culture.label: Day names
culture.text: Akan children are named for the day they were born — Kofi for a Friday boy, Ama for a Saturday girl.

culture.label: Football
culture.text: The Black Stars are followed everywhere, and Ghana was the first African side to reach a World Cup quarter-final in 2010.

talkAbout: Jollof — Ghana's position is that it wins.
Kente and what the patterns mean.
Being first to independence, and Nkrumah's legacy.
avoid: The slave forts are places of mourning, not attractions. Ethnic and chieftaincy politics need care.

people.name: Julius Nyerere
people.why: Led independence, promoted Swahili as a unifying language, and stepped down voluntarily.

people.name: Freddie Mercury
people.why: Born in Zanzibar; Queen's frontman and one of rock's greatest voices.

people.name: Abdulrazak Gurnah
people.why: Zanzibar-born winner of the 2021 Nobel Prize in Literature.

people.name: Bi Kidude
people.why: The queen of taarab music, still performing into her nineties.

people.name: Samia Suluhu Hassan
people.why: Tanzania's first woman president, from Zanzibar.

events.title: The Swahili coast
events.what: Kilwa and Zanzibar were rich Indian Ocean trading cities where Swahili culture formed.

events.title: The Maji Maji rebellion
events.what: A rising against German rule crushed with a scorched-earth campaign that killed perhaps 300,000.

events.title: Independence and union
events.what: Tanganyika became independent and then united with Zanzibar to form Tanzania.

events.title: The Laetoli footprints
events.what: 3.6-million-year-old hominin footprints found in Tanzania, showing upright walking.

culture.label: Swahili
culture.text: Deliberately promoted after independence as a national language above ethnic ones; it worked.

culture.label: Kilimanjaro
culture.text: Africa's highest mountain, walkable to the summit without technical climbing.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Ugali, nyama choma, and Zanzibar's spiced pilau and biryani.

culture.label: Taarab & bongo flava
culture.text: Zanzibari taarab with Arab and Indian influences, and the mainland's hip-hop-derived bongo flava.

culture.label: Serengeti
culture.text: The migration and Ngorongoro crater hold some of the densest wildlife populations anywhere.

talkAbout: Swahili, and how it unified the country.
avoid: Mainland–Zanzibar politics is sensitive. Don't assume Tanzania is only safari and beaches.

people.name: Albert Camus
people.why: Born in Algeria, Nobel laureate, and inseparable from the Algerian landscape he wrote about.

people.name: Emir Abdelkader
people.why: Led the resistance to French conquest and later protected Damascus's Christians from massacre.

people.name: Djamila Bouhired
people.why: A fighter in the Battle of Algiers whose trial made her a symbol of the independence war.

people.name: Assia Djebar
people.why: The first North African woman elected to the Académie française.

people.name: Zinedine Zidane
people.why: Of Algerian Kabyle descent, and one of the greatest footballers of his generation.

events.title: The French invasion
events.what: The start of 132 years of colonial rule, and of settlement that displaced Algerians from their land.

events.title: The war of independence
events.what: Eight years of war, with torture and mass casualties, ending French rule.

events.title: The black decade
events.what: A civil war between the state and Islamist groups killed around 200,000 people.

events.title: The Hirak
events.what: Millions marched peacefully every Friday for a year and forced Bouteflika from office.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Couscous — UNESCO-listed across the Maghreb — chorba soup, and pastries drenched in honey.

culture.label: Raï
culture.text: Born in Oran, blending Bedouin song with Western pop; it travelled to France and beyond.

culture.label: Sahara
culture.text: Africa's largest country, four-fifths desert, with the Tassili n'Ajjer rock art going back 12,000 years.

culture.label: Amazigh
culture.text: Tamazight is an official language, and Kabyle identity is strongly asserted.

culture.label: Cafés
culture.text: Long hours over coffee and conversation, especially in Algiers.

talkAbout: The Sahara and the rock art.
avoid: The war of independence and the 1990s civil war are both raw. Politics is closely watched.

people.name: Léopold Sédar Senghor
people.why: A founder of Négritude, the first president, and the first African in the Académie française.

people.name: Youssou N'Dour
people.why: Took mbalax to the world and was later Senegal's culture minister.

people.name: Ousmane Sembène
people.why: The father of African cinema, who made films so people who could not read could hear his stories.

people.name: Mariama Bâ
people.why: So Long a Letter is one of the most taught African novels on women's lives.

people.name: Sadio Mané
people.why: Champions League winner who led Senegal to its first Africa Cup of Nations title.

events.title: Gorée Island
events.what: A slave-trading post off Dakar, now a memorial and World Heritage site.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Senegal left French rule under Senghor and has never had a military coup.

events.title: The World Festival of Negro Arts
events.what: Dakar hosted a landmark gathering of Black artists and thinkers from across the world.

events.title: Africa Cup of Nations
events.what: Senegal won its first continental title, and the country celebrated for days.

culture.label: Teranga
culture.text: Senegalese hospitality is a point of national identity; a guest is fed before anything else.

culture.label: Thieboudienne
culture.text: Fish and rice cooked in tomato — the national dish, and UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Mbalax
culture.text: Driven by the sabar drum, and the sound of Dakar's clubs.

culture.label: Laamb
culture.text: Traditional wrestling with striking allowed; bigger than football in ticket sales.

culture.label: Sufi brotherhoods
culture.text: The Mouride and Tijani orders shape religious and economic life; Touba draws millions.

avoid: Gorée and the slave trade are subjects for respect, not curiosity. Religious brotherhoods and politics are intertwined and sensitive.

people.name: Hannibal Barca
people.why: Crossed the Alps with elephants and nearly destroyed Rome; born in Carthage.

people.name: Habib Bourguiba
people.why: Led Tunisia to independence and gave women legal rights unmatched in the region at the time.

people.name: Ibn Khaldun
people.why: The Muqaddimah founded historiography and, arguably, sociology.

people.name: Mohamed Bouazizi
people.why: His self-immolation set off the Tunisian revolution and then the Arab Spring.

people.name: Ons Jabeur
people.why: The first Arab and African woman to reach a Grand Slam final.

events.title: Carthage
events.what: A Phoenician city that became Rome's great rival, and was destroyed for it.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Tunisia left French rule; the following year's Code of Personal Status transformed women's rights.

events.title: The revolution
events.what: Protests removed Ben Ali after 23 years and began the Arab Spring.

events.title: The Nobel Peace Prize
events.what: Awarded to the National Dialogue Quartet for pulling the country back from civil conflict.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Harissa in everything, brik pastry with a runny egg, and couscous on Fridays.

culture.label: Roman ruins
culture.text: El Djem's amphitheatre held 35,000 people and is among the best preserved anywhere.

culture.label: Tea
culture.text: Mint tea with pine nuts, taken slowly in cafés.

culture.label: Film sets
culture.text: Southern Tunisia stood in for Tatooine; the sets are still there.

culture.label: Languages
culture.text: Tunisian Arabic mixed with French, and Amazigh still spoken in the south.

talkAbout: The revolution, which Tunisians view with mixed feelings.
avoid: The political and economic situation since 2011 is a source of real frustration. Migration across the Mediterranean is a painful subject.

people.name: Omar Mukhtar
people.why: Led twenty years of resistance to Italian occupation before being hanged at 73.

people.name: Ibrahim al-Koni
people.why: One of the Arab world's most prolific novelists, writing the Sahara and Tuareg life.

people.name: Hisham Matar
people.why: The Return, about his father's disappearance under Gaddafi, won the Pulitzer Prize.

people.name: Idris I
people.why: Libya's only king, who led it to independence in 1951 and was deposed in 1969.

people.name: Khaled Mattawa
people.why: Has translated much of modern Arabic poetry into English and won a MacArthur fellowship.

events.title: Cyrene and Leptis Magna
events.what: Greek and Roman cities on the Libyan coast, among the finest classical ruins in the Mediterranean.

events.title: Italian rule
events.what: Colonisation and a brutal counter-insurgency that killed a large share of the population of Cyrenaica.

events.title: Gaddafi
events.what: Forty-two years of idiosyncratic personal rule funded by oil.

events.title: The uprising
events.what: Protests became a civil war and NATO intervention; Gaddafi was killed, and instability followed.

culture.label: Sahara
culture.text: Ninety per cent desert, with the Acacus mountains holding prehistoric rock art.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Bazin, a barley dough eaten with lamb sauce, and a Libyan take on couscous.

culture.label: Ruins
culture.text: Leptis Magna is often called the best-preserved Roman city outside Italy.

culture.label: Tea
culture.text: Strong green tea with peanuts, poured three times, each pour a different strength.

culture.label: Tuareg
culture.text: Tuareg and Tebu communities in the south have their own languages and traditions.

avoid: Libya has been divided by conflict since 2011 and politics is dangerous ground. Many Libyans have lost family or been displaced.

people.name: Tayeb Salih
people.why: Season of Migration to the North is one of the finest Arabic novels of the twentieth century.

people.name: Alaa Salah
people.why: Photographed standing on a car leading chants in 2019; she became the image of the revolution.

people.name: Muhammad Ahmad
people.why: Led the revolt that took Khartoum and created an independent Sudanese state.

people.name: Ibrahim El-Salahi
people.why: A pioneer of African modernism whose work is in the Tate and MoMA.

people.name: Mohammed Wardi
people.why: Sudan's most beloved musician, repeatedly exiled for his political songs.

events.title: The Kingdom of Kush
events.what: Nubian kings ruled Egypt as its 25th dynasty; Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt does.

events.title: The Mahdist state
events.what: A revolt drove out Egyptian and British forces and ruled Sudan for over a decade.

events.title: Darfur
events.what: Government-backed militias carried out killings that the US and others called genocide.

events.title: The revolution
events.what: Months of protest ended Omar al-Bashir's thirty-year rule.

culture.label: Pyramids
culture.text: Meroë has around 200 steep-sided Nubian pyramids, far more than Egypt and far fewer visitors.

culture.label: Hospitality
culture.text: Legendary even by regional standards; strangers are routinely fed and housed.

culture.label: Jebena
culture.text: Coffee spiced with ginger and cardamom, poured from a clay pot through a grass filter.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Sudanese music blends Arab and African forms, with the oud and the tambour.

culture.label: The Niles
culture.text: The Blue and White Nile meet at Khartoum, visibly two different colours.

avoid: The current war has displaced more people than any other conflict on earth. Almost every Sudanese abroad has family in danger.

people.name: Félix Houphouët-Boigny
people.why: Led the country from independence for 33 years and built the world's largest church at Yamoussoukro.

people.name: Didier Drogba
people.why: A Champions League winner who publicly appealed for a ceasefire in the civil war — and got one.

people.name: Ahmadou Kourouma
people.why: Wrote French as it is actually spoken in West Africa, and won the Prix Renaudot.

people.name: Alpha Blondy
people.why: Africa's biggest reggae star, singing in Dioula, French and English.

people.name: Marie-Josée Ta Lou
people.why: World champion and the country's most successful track athlete.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Côte d'Ivoire left French rule and became West Africa's economic powerhouse through cocoa.

events.title: Capital moved
events.what: Houphouët-Boigny moved the capital to his home village of Yamoussoukro, though Abidjan remains the real centre.

events.title: The civil wars
events.what: Two conflicts divided the country north and south before reunification.

events.title: Cocoa
events.what: Côte d'Ivoire produces around 40% of the world's cocoa, with all the leverage and problems that brings.

culture.label: Cocoa
culture.text: The world's largest producer, though most Ivorians rarely eat chocolate.

culture.label: Coupé-décalé
culture.text: A dance music born in the Ivorian diaspora in Paris and now dominant in Abidjan clubs.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Attiéké — fermented cassava couscous — with grilled fish, and kedjenou chicken.

culture.label: Masks
culture.text: Dan, Baoulé and Senufo mask traditions are among West Africa's most celebrated.

culture.label: Football
culture.text: The Elephants won the Africa Cup of Nations at home in 2024 after an unlikely run.

talkAbout: Football and the 2024 Cup of Nations.
avoid: The civil wars and the politics of ivoirité — who counts as truly Ivorian — remain divisive.

people.name: Mansa Musa
people.why: Ruled the Mali Empire and is often estimated the wealthiest person in recorded history.

people.name: Salif Keita
people.why: The Golden Voice of Africa, a descendant of Mali's founding king who became a singer despite it.

people.name: Ali Farka Touré
people.why: Showed that the blues came from here; won Grammys for his desert guitar.

people.name: Sundiata Keita
people.why: Founded the Mali Empire; his epic is still performed by griots.

people.name: Oumou Sangaré
people.why: The voice of Wassoulou music and an outspoken campaigner on women's rights.

events.title: The Mali Empire
events.what: One of the wealthiest states of its era, controlling the gold and salt trade across the Sahara.

events.title: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage
events.what: He gave away so much gold in Cairo that he depressed its value for a decade.

events.title: Timbuktu
events.what: A centre of scholarship with hundreds of thousands of manuscripts, many still preserved.

events.title: The northern crisis
events.what: A Tuareg rebellion and jihadist takeover of the north; manuscripts were smuggled out of Timbuktu to save them.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Mali is one of the great music countries on earth — kora, ngoni and desert guitar.

culture.label: Manuscripts
culture.text: Timbuktu's libraries held astronomy, law and medicine written centuries ago in Arabic and Songhai.

culture.label: Djenné
culture.text: The Great Mosque is the largest mud-brick building in the world and is replastered by the town each year.

culture.label: Griots
culture.text: Hereditary musician-historians who hold family and national memory and perform it.

culture.label: Joking cousins
culture.text: Sanankuya lets certain families insult each other freely — a genuine mechanism for defusing tension.

talkAbout: Music, which Malians rightly consider world-class.
The Mali Empire and Timbuktu's manuscripts.
The joking-cousin tradition, which visitors find remarkable.
avoid: The conflict in the north and centre, and the current government's alignments, are dangerous topics.

people.name: Hamani Diori
people.why: Niger's first president after independence, in office for fourteen years.

people.name: Mamar Kassey
people.why: Brought Nigerien Songhai and Fulani music to international audiences.

people.name: Bibata Niandou Barry
people.why: A leading advocate for women's political representation in Niger.

people.name: Mano Dayak
people.why: Led the Tuareg rebellion and then negotiated its peace before dying in a plane crash.

people.name: Rahmatou Keïta
people.why: The first Nigerien woman to direct a feature film, shown at international festivals.

events.title: Agadez and the trans-Saharan trade
events.what: A caravan city where salt, gold and slaves crossed the desert.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Niger left French rule as one of the world's poorest countries by income.

events.title: The Tuareg rebellions
events.what: Northern uprisings over marginalisation, settled by negotiated peace agreements.

events.title: The coup
events.what: The army removed the elected president, and Niger joined its neighbours in the Alliance of Sahel States.

culture.label: Salt caravans
culture.text: The azalai caravans still carry salt from Bilma across the desert by camel.

culture.label: Gerewol
culture.text: Wodaabe men wear elaborate makeup and dance for hours while women choose partners.

culture.label: Regreening
culture.text: Farmers have brought back millions of trees across the Sahel through natural regeneration.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Millet porridge, rice with peanut sauce, and grilled meat with spiced pepper mix.

culture.label: Giraffes
culture.text: The last West African giraffes live near Kouré and have been brought back from near extinction.

talkAbout: The Gerewol festival and Wodaabe traditions.
The regreening of the Sahel, which is a genuine success story.
avoid: Politics since the 2023 coup, and the jihadist insurgency, are dangerous subjects. Niger is frequently confused with Nigeria — don't.

people.name: Ahmed Sékou Touré
people.why: Told de Gaulle Guinea preferred poverty in freedom to riches in slavery, and took independence in 1958.

people.name: Mory Kanté
people.why: 'Yé ké yé ké' was the first African single to sell a million copies.

people.name: Camara Laye
people.why: The African Child is one of the founding texts of Francophone African literature.

people.name: Sory Kandia Kouyaté
people.why: A griot whose voice defined the sound of post-independence Guinea.

people.name: Naby Keïta
people.why: A Champions League and Premier League winner, and Guinea's best-known athlete.

events.title: The Imamate of Futa Jallon
events.what: One of West Africa's earliest Islamic states, in the highlands.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Guinea was the only French colony to vote no to de Gaulle's community; France withdrew everything overnight.

events.title: Les Ballets Africains
events.what: The state-backed national ensemble brought Guinean dance and drumming to world stages.

events.title: The Ebola outbreak
events.what: The West African epidemic began in Guinea and killed thousands across the region.

culture.label: Djembe
culture.text: The drum is Guinean in origin, and its playing traditions are among the most respected in Africa.

culture.label: Futa Jallon
culture.text: Highlands where the Niger, Senegal and Gambia rivers all rise — the water tower of West Africa.

culture.label: Bauxite
culture.text: Guinea holds the world's largest reserves of the ore aluminium is made from.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Rice with peanut or leaf sauce, and fouti — Guinea's take on the West African staple.

culture.label: Griots
culture.text: Mande griot families carry centuries of history in song and are still consulted.

talkAbout: Drumming and dance, which Guinea is famous for.
avoid: Coups and political instability are recent and ongoing. The 2009 stadium massacre is a serious subject.

people.name: Bai Bureh
people.why: Led the Hut Tax War against British rule and is on the banknotes.

people.name: Salone's Refugee All Stars
people.why: Formed in a refugee camp during the civil war and toured the world afterwards.

people.name: Ishmael Beah
people.why: A Long Way Gone, his memoir of being a child soldier, was read worldwide.

people.name: Constance Cummings-John
people.why: One of the first women elected in colonial Africa, and mayor of Freetown.

people.name: Mohamed Kallon
people.why: Sierra Leone's most successful footballer, who played in Serie A.

events.title: The Province of Freedom
events.what: Freetown was founded as a settlement for freed slaves from Britain, Nova Scotia and Jamaica.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Sierra Leone left British rule.

events.title: The civil war
events.what: Eleven years of war funded by diamonds, with mass amputations and child soldiers.

events.title: Ebola
events.what: Nearly 4,000 people died, and the health system was rebuilt around what was learned.

culture.label: Krio
culture.text: An English-based creole spoken by nearly everyone, and the language of Freetown.

culture.label: Cotton Tree
culture.text: The tree freed slaves gathered under in Freetown stood until 2023 and was the city's symbol.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Cassava leaf and groundnut stew over rice; rice is considered the only real meal.

culture.label: Masquerade
culture.text: Devil masquerades appear at celebrations, each society with its own figures.

culture.label: Beaches
culture.text: The peninsula's white-sand beaches are among the finest and least visited in West Africa.

talkAbout: Krio and how much of it a visitor can pick up.
avoid: The civil war and 'blood diamonds' are traumatic for a generation, not a film plot. Ebola is recent.

people.name: Angélique Kidjo
people.why: Five Grammy Awards and one of the most recognisable African voices in the world.

people.name: Béhanzin
people.why: The last independent king of Dahomey, who fought the French and died in exile.

people.name: Mathieu Kérékou
people.why: Ruled as a Marxist, then lost an election, accepted it, and later won one back.

people.name: Nafissatou Thiam
people.why: Of Beninese descent, a double Olympic champion in the heptathlon.

people.name: Romuald Hazoumè
people.why: Makes masks from discarded jerrycans; his work is in the British Museum.

events.title: The Kingdom of Dahomey
events.what: A powerful state with an all-female military corps, and a major participant in the slave trade.

events.title: Ouidah
events.what: One of the busiest slave ports on the coast; the Door of No Return stands on the beach.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Dahomey left French rule, renaming itself Benin in 1975.

events.title: The national conference
events.what: Benin invented the African national conference, moving peacefully from Marxism to multiparty democracy.

culture.label: Vodun
culture.text: Vodou originated here and is an official religion, with a national holiday on 10 January.

culture.label: Ganvié
culture.text: A village of 20,000 people built on stilts in a lagoon, reached only by boat.

culture.label: The Agojie
culture.text: Dahomey's women warriors, active for two centuries and the subject of recent films.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Pâte with sauce, akassa, and plenty of grilled fish along the coast.

culture.label: Egungun
culture.text: Masqueraders representing ancestors appear at festivals in spectacular layered costumes.

talkAbout: Vodun as a living religion, quite unlike its film version.
avoid: Dahomey's role in the slave trade is complicated and discussed carefully. Vodun deserves respect, not spooky references.

people.name: Sylvanus Olympio
people.why: Led Togo to independence and was killed in Africa's first post-independence military coup.

people.name: Emmanuel Adebayor
people.why: African Footballer of the Year and Togo's most famous sportsman.

people.name: Tété-Michel Kpomassie
people.why: Read a book about Greenland as a boy, spent years travelling there, and wrote a classic about it.

people.name: Bella Bellow
people.why: Togo's most celebrated voice, who died in a car crash at 27.

people.name: Kossi Efoui
people.why: A playwright and novelist in exile whose work won major Francophone prizes.

events.title: German Togoland
events.what: Germany called it its model colony; the railways and cocoa plantations date from then.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Togo left French trusteeship under Olympio.

events.title: Eyadéma
events.what: Gnassingbé Eyadéma ruled for 38 years, one of Africa's longest-serving leaders.

events.title: The Nations Cup
events.what: Togo qualified for its first and so far only World Cup, a national landmark.

culture.label: Koutammakou
culture.text: The Batammariba build tower-houses of mud and wood; the landscape is World Heritage-listed.

culture.label: Vodun
culture.text: Lomé's fetish market supplies practitioners across the region.

culture.label: Nana Benz
culture.text: Women traders who dominated the West African wax-print cloth trade and became famously wealthy.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Fufu and pâte with palm nut or groundnut sauce, and akpan fermented maize drink.

culture.label: Coast
culture.text: A narrow country, 56 km of coast but stretching 550 km inland to the savanna.

talkAbout: The Nana Benz and the cloth trade.
avoid: The Gnassingbé family has ruled for over fifty years and politics is sensitive. Vodun is a religion, not a curiosity.

people.name: Thomas Sankara
people.why: Africa's Che Guevara — renamed the country, sold the government's Mercedes fleet, and was assassinated at 37.

people.name: Idrissa Ouédraogo
people.why: Won the Grand Prix at Cannes with Tilaï, and helped make Ouagadougou Africa's film capital.

people.name: Gaston Kaboré
people.why: Wend Kuuni is a landmark of African cinema, told almost without dialogue.

people.name: Amadou Hampâté Bâ
people.why: Said that when an old man dies in Africa, a library burns — and spent his life preventing it.

people.name: Smockey
people.why: Co-founded Le Balai Citoyen, the movement that helped bring down Compaoré in 2014.

events.title: The Mossi kingdoms
events.what: States that resisted both the Mali and Songhai empires for centuries.

events.title: Sankara's revolution
events.what: Land reform, mass vaccination, banning forced marriage, and renaming Upper Volta 'land of upright people'.

events.title: FESPACO founded
events.what: Africa's largest film festival has been held in Ouagadougou every two years since.

events.title: The uprising
events.what: Protesters burned parliament and ended Blaise Compaoré's 27 years in power.

culture.label: FESPACO
culture.text: The continent's most important film festival, and the reason Ouagadougou matters in world cinema.

culture.label: Masks
culture.text: Bwa and Bobo plank masks, several metres tall, danced at harvest and funerals.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Tô, a millet or sorghum dough, with baobab-leaf or okra sauce; riz gras on special days.

culture.label: Balafon
culture.text: The wooden xylophone with gourd resonators; the Sambla and Tusia traditions are UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Integrity
culture.text: The country's name means 'land of upright people', and Burkinabè take the idea seriously.

avoid: The jihadist insurgency has displaced millions and politics since the 2022 coups is dangerous ground.

people.name: Dawda Jawara
people.why: A vet who led The Gambia to independence and governed for nearly thirty years.

people.name: Kunta Kinteh
people.why: Alex Haley traced Roots to a Gambian village, bringing the diaspora back to the river.

people.name: Foday Musa Suso
people.why: A griot who brought the kora into collaborations with Herbie Hancock and Philip Glass.

people.name: Fatou Bensouda
people.why: Chief Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court from 2012 to 2021.

people.name: Sona Jobarteh
people.why: The first woman from a griot family to become a professional kora player.

events.title: The river colony
events.what: European powers fought over the Gambia River as a trade route deep into West Africa.

events.title: Independence
events.what: The Gambia left British rule, becoming Africa's smallest mainland country.

events.title: The Jammeh years
events.what: Yahya Jammeh seized power at 29 and ruled for 22 increasingly repressive years.

events.title: The peaceful transition
events.what: Jammeh lost an election and, after regional pressure, left — a rare orderly handover.

culture.label: Kora
culture.text: The 21-string harp-lute, played by hereditary griot families across the Mande world.

culture.label: The river
culture.text: The country is essentially a strip of land either side of one river, 30 km wide at most.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Benachin — the ancestor of jollof rice — and domoda groundnut stew.

culture.label: Birds
culture.text: Over 500 species in a tiny country; birdwatchers come from everywhere.

culture.label: Smiling Coast
culture.text: The tourist slogan, but Gambians do treat friendliness as a matter of national character.

talkAbout: Roots, and diaspora visitors coming back.
avoid: The Jammeh era, including disappearances and his HIV 'cure' claims, is painful. Migration by boat to Europe has cost many young lives.

people.name: Milton Obote
people.why: Led Uganda to independence and returned to power after Amin, twice ending badly.

people.name: Janani Luwum
people.why: Criticised Idi Amin publicly and was killed for it; his statue stands at Westminster Abbey.

people.name: Stephen Kiprotich
people.why: Won Olympic gold in 2012, only Uganda's second ever.

people.name: Okot p'Bitek
people.why: Song of Lawino is one of the great works of African poetry in English.

people.name: Joshua Cheptegei
people.why: World record holder at 5,000 and 10,000 metres, and Olympic champion.

events.title: The Kingdom of Buganda
events.what: A centralised kingdom on Lake Victoria that still exists as a cultural institution.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Uganda left British rule; Churchill had called it the Pearl of Africa.

events.title: Idi Amin
events.what: Eight years of terror, the expulsion of the Asian community, and perhaps 300,000 dead.

events.title: The Lord's Resistance Army
events.what: A northern insurgency that abducted tens of thousands of children as soldiers.

culture.label: Matoke
culture.text: Steamed green banana mashed into the staple food, served with groundnut sauce.

culture.label: Gorillas
culture.text: Bwindi holds about half the world's remaining mountain gorillas.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: From the adungu harp to a thriving Kampala Afrobeats and dancehall scene.

culture.label: Kingdoms
culture.text: Buganda, Bunyoro, Toro and Busoga survive as cultural kingdoms with their own kings.

culture.label: Rolex
culture.text: Not a watch — an omelette rolled in a chapati, invented as student food and now everywhere.

talkAbout: The rolex, which delights every visitor.
The kingdoms, and which one someone belongs to.
avoid: The Amin years, LGBTQ rights legislation and long-running politics are all sensitive.

people.name: Paul Rusesabagina
people.why: Sheltered over a thousand people at the Hôtel des Mille Collines; the subject of Hotel Rwanda.

people.name: Immaculée Ilibagiza
people.why: Survived 91 days hidden in a bathroom during the genocide and wrote about forgiveness.

people.name: King Mutara III Rudahigwa
people.why: Abolished ubuhake serfdom and pushed for independence from Belgium.

people.name: Dian Fossey
people.why: Spent eighteen years studying mountain gorillas in Rwanda and was murdered there.

people.name: Adrien Niyonshuti
people.why: Lost six brothers in the genocide and became Rwanda's first Olympic mountain biker.

events.title: Colonial rule
events.what: German then Belgian administration hardened Hutu and Tutsi into fixed racial categories with identity cards.

events.title: The genocide
events.what: Around 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu were killed in a hundred days while the world stood by.

events.title: The gacaca courts
events.what: Community courts tried around two million cases the formal system could never have handled.

events.title: Women in parliament
events.what: Rwanda became the first country in the world with a majority-women legislature.

culture.label: Umuganda
culture.text: The last Saturday of each month, the whole country does community work; everything closes.

culture.label: Gorillas
culture.text: Volcanoes National Park holds mountain gorillas, and each infant is named in a public ceremony.

culture.label: Agaseke
culture.text: The peace basket, woven in a tight spiral with a conical lid, given at weddings.

culture.label: Thousand hills
culture.text: The whole country is terraced hillside; the roads are almost never straight.

culture.label: Plastic ban
culture.text: Rwanda banned plastic bags in 2008 and Kigali is among the cleanest cities anywhere.

talkAbout: Coffee and tea, which are excellent.
avoid: The genocide is remembered openly at Kwibuka each April, but is not small talk. Ethnic labels are legally and socially discouraged.

people.name: Sayyid Mohammed Abdullah Hassan
people.why: Fought British, Italian and Ethiopian forces for twenty years and was a considerable poet.

people.name: Nuruddin Farah
people.why: Somalia's foremost novelist, writing in English from decades of exile.

people.name: Waris Dirie
people.why: A nomad who became a supermodel and then the leading global campaigner against FGM.

people.name: Ilhan Omar
people.why: A refugee from Mogadishu who became one of the first Muslim women in the US Congress.

people.name: Hodan Nalayeh
people.why: Reported on ordinary Somali life against the news stereotype; killed in an attack in Kismayo.

events.title: The Ajuran Sultanate
events.what: A powerful Indian Ocean state that built stone wells and fought off the Portuguese.

events.title: Independence and union
events.what: British Somaliland and Italian Somaliland became independent days apart and united.

events.title: State collapse
events.what: Siad Barre fell and central government effectively ceased for two decades.

events.title: A federal government
events.what: The first permanent central government since 1991 was formed in Mogadishu.

culture.label: Poetry
culture.text: Somalis are sometimes called a nation of poets; verse carries politics, feuds and reconciliation.

culture.label: Camels
culture.text: Somalia has more camels than any country on earth, and they measure wealth and status.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Bariis with goat, sambusa, and a banana served alongside the main course.

culture.label: Shaah
culture.text: Spiced tea with cardamom and cinnamon, drunk sweet and constantly.

culture.label: Clan
culture.text: Clan lineage organises much of social life, and people can recite generations of ancestry.

talkAbout: The diaspora — Somalis are spread across the world and stay connected.
avoid: Clan politics, al-Shabaab and Somaliland's status are all delicate. Piracy jokes are unwelcome.

people.name: Isaias Afwerki
people.why: Led the independence struggle and has ruled without elections ever since 1993.

people.name: Bereket Mengisteab
people.why: A krar player whose songs carried the independence movement for decades.

people.name: Daniel Teklehaimanot
people.why: The first Eritrean and first Black African to wear the polka-dot jersey at the Tour de France.

people.name: Zeresenay Alemseged
people.why: Discovered 'Selam', a 3.3-million-year-old child fossil, the most complete of its kind.

people.name: Sulieman Ahmed
people.why: Part of the generation that made Eritrea the strongest cycling nation in Africa.

events.title: Italian Eritrea
events.what: Colonial rule left Asmara's modernist architecture, now World Heritage-listed.

events.title: The war of independence
events.what: Thirty years of war against Ethiopia, one of Africa's longest.

events.title: Independence
events.what: A referendum confirmed independence by over 99%.

events.title: Peace with Ethiopia
events.what: A twenty-year frozen conflict formally ended, winning Ethiopia's prime minister a Nobel Prize.

culture.label: Asmara
culture.text: An Italian modernist city on a plateau, complete with a 1930s petrol station shaped like an aeroplane.

culture.label: Cycling
culture.text: An Italian legacy that stuck; Eritrea is the strongest cycling country in Africa.

culture.label: Coffee ceremony
culture.text: As in Ethiopia — roasted, ground and served in three rounds over an hour or more.

culture.label: Injera
culture.text: Shared from one platter with zigni stew, and Italian pasta alongside it in Asmara.

culture.label: Nine groups
culture.text: Nine recognised ethnic groups and languages, with Tigrinya, Arabic and English in official use.

talkAbout: Cycling, which Eritrea dominates on the continent.
Coffee and food, shared with Ethiopia.
avoid: Indefinite national service drives large-scale emigration and is a serious grievance. Politics is dangerous to discuss.

people.name: Hassan Gouled Aptidon
people.why: Led Djibouti to independence in 1977 and was its first president.

people.name: Abdourahman Waberi
people.why: Djibouti's best-known writer, published in French and widely translated.

people.name: Ahmed Salah
people.why: Won Djibouti's only Olympic medal, a marathon bronze in 1988.

people.name: Ayanleh Souleiman
people.why: World indoor champion and multiple medallist over 800 and 1500 metres.

people.name: Zahra Ahmed Abdillahi
people.why: A leading voice against female genital mutilation in the Horn of Africa.

events.title: French Somaliland
events.what: France took the port to compete with British-held Aden across the strait.

events.title: The Addis Ababa railway
events.what: The line to the Ethiopian capital made Djibouti the region's port and still does.

events.title: Independence
events.what: One of the last African colonies to become independent.

events.title: The bases
events.what: France, the US, China, Japan and others all keep military bases here, on the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.

culture.label: Lake Assal
culture.text: The lowest point in Africa and one of the saltiest bodies of water on earth.

culture.label: Khat
culture.text: Afternoon chews structure the day; flights bringing it from Ethiopia arrive daily.

culture.label: Whale sharks
culture.text: The Gulf of Tadjoura is one of the reliable places in the world to swim with them.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Somali, Afar, Yemeni and French influences — skoudehkaris rice, and good baguettes.

culture.label: The strait
culture.text: A third of world shipping passes the Bab-el-Mandeb, which is Djibouti's whole strategic value.

talkAbout: Lake Assal and the volcanic landscape.
The port, and how a small country sits on a global chokepoint.
avoid: Domestic politics is closed. Ethnic balance between Issa and Afar communities is sensitive.

people.name: Roger Milla
people.why: Scored at 38 in the 1990 World Cup and danced at the corner flag; the first African team in a quarter-final.

people.name: Manu Dibango
people.why: 'Soul Makossa' is one of the foundational records of disco and hip-hop sampling.

people.name: Samuel Eto'o
people.why: Four-time African Player of the Year and a treble winner with Barcelona and Inter.

people.name: Ruben Um Nyobè
people.why: Led the UPC independence movement and was killed by French forces.

people.name: Calixthe Beyala
people.why: A prolific and provocative writer on African women's lives, published across the Francophone world.

events.title: German Kamerun
events.what: German colonisation, ending when Britain and France divided the territory in the First World War.

events.title: The hidden war
events.what: France fought a long counter-insurgency against the UPC independence movement, only recently acknowledged.

events.title: Independence and union
events.what: French Cameroun became independent, and part of British Cameroons voted to join it.

events.title: The Anglophone crisis
events.what: Protests by English-speaking lawyers and teachers escalated into a separatist conflict.

culture.label: Africa in miniature
culture.text: Desert, savanna, rainforest, mountains and coast, plus around 250 languages, in one country.

culture.label: Indomitable Lions
culture.text: Five Africa Cup of Nations titles and the team that broke through in 1990.

culture.label: Makossa & bikutsi
culture.text: Two Cameroonian styles that shaped African popular music.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Ndolé — bitterleaf with peanuts and fish — is the national dish, plus grilled fish and plantain.

culture.label: Chiefdoms
culture.text: The Bamiléké and Bamum kingdoms in the west retain palaces and their own royal art.

avoid: The Anglophone conflict, Biya's long rule and the colonial war are all sensitive and current.

people.name: Patrice Lumumba
people.why: The country's first elected leader, assassinated within months with foreign involvement.

people.name: Denis Mukwege
people.why: Has treated tens of thousands of survivors of wartime sexual violence; Nobel Peace Prize, 2018.

people.name: Franco Luambo
people.why: The Sorcerer of the Guitar, whose TPOK Jazz defined Congolese rumba for thirty years.

people.name: Papa Wemba
people.why: The king of soukous and a leader of the sapeur dandy movement.

people.name: Chérie Rivers
people.why: Congolese-American scholar writing on how the world looks at Congo's suffering.

events.title: The Congo Free State
events.what: Leopold II ran the territory as private property; millions died under forced rubber collection.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Lumumba's independence speech to the Belgian king is still quoted across Africa.

events.title: The Rumble in the Jungle
events.what: Ali beat Foreman in Kinshasa in front of 60,000 people.

events.title: The Congo wars
events.what: Africa's world war drew in nine countries and killed millions, mostly from disease and hunger.

culture.label: Rumba
culture.text: Congolese rumba is UNESCO-listed and has been the dominant sound of African music for decades.

culture.label: Sapeurs
culture.text: La Sape — men in immaculate designer suits treating elegance as a form of dignity.

culture.label: Rainforest
culture.text: The Congo Basin is the world's second-largest rainforest and a critical carbon sink.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Fufu with pondu cassava leaves, moambe chicken, and grilled river fish.

culture.label: Cobalt
culture.text: Around 70% of the world's cobalt comes from here, much of it under harsh conditions.

talkAbout: Music — Congolese rumba is a genuine world treasure.
avoid: The eastern conflict, mining conditions and Belgian colonial atrocities are heavy subjects. Don't confuse the DRC with Republic of the Congo.

people.name: Omar Bongo
people.why: Ruled for 41 years, one of the longest tenures of any head of state in the world.

people.name: Albert Schweitzer
people.why: Founded the hospital at Lambaréné and won the Nobel Peace Prize for his work there.

people.name: Pierre Akendengué
people.why: Gabon's most respected songwriter, blending Myene traditions with political lyricism.

people.name: Angèle Ondo
people.why: A leading voice in contemporary Gabonese music.

people.name: Daniel Cousin
people.why: Gabon's record scorer for years and its most prominent player in Europe.

events.title: French Gabon
events.what: Libreville was founded as a settlement for freed slaves, hence its name.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Gabon left French rule, retaining unusually close ties to Paris.

events.title: Thirteen national parks
events.what: Gabon set aside 11% of its territory for conservation in a single stroke.

events.title: The coup
events.what: The army ended 56 years of Bongo family rule.

culture.label: Forest
culture.text: Nearly 90% forest cover, with forest elephants, gorillas and surfing hippos at Loango.

culture.label: Bwiti
culture.text: A spiritual tradition using iboga, with all-night ceremonies of music and dance.

culture.label: Ngombi
culture.text: The sacred harp of Bwiti ritual, carved with a human figure.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Nyembwe chicken in palm nut sauce, and plenty of river and sea fish.

culture.label: Libreville
culture.text: 'Free town', founded for people liberated from a slave ship in 1849.

talkAbout: The national parks and forest wildlife.
Football and the Africa Cup of Nations.
avoid: The Bongo dynasty and the 2023 coup are current politics. Oil wealth and inequality are sensitive.

people.name: François Tombalbaye
people.why: Chad's first president after independence, killed in a coup.

people.name: Mahamat-Saleh Haroun
people.why: A Screaming Man won the Jury Prize at Cannes, the first Chadian film in competition.

people.name: Hissène Habré
people.why: Convicted of crimes against humanity in Senegal — the first African leader tried in another African country.

people.name: Jacqueline Moudeina
people.why: Survived a grenade attack and spent years building the case that convicted Habré.

people.name: Djimon Hounsou
people.why: Twice Oscar-nominated; born in Benin but of Chadian and West African Fon heritage.

events.title: The green Sahara
events.what: Rock art in the Ennedi shows cattle and swimmers where there is now only desert.

events.title: French Chad
events.what: Colonised late and administered lightly; independence came in 1960.

events.title: The Toyota War
events.what: Chadian forces in pickup trucks defeated Libyan armour, one of the great asymmetric victories.

events.title: The Habré verdict
events.what: A landmark for international justice: an African court convicting a former African head of state.

culture.label: Ennedi
culture.text: Sandstone arches and gorges in the desert, with prehistoric rock art and a relict crocodile population.

culture.label: Lake Chad
culture.text: Once one of Africa's largest lakes, now a fraction of its 1960s size.

culture.label: Wodaabe
culture.text: Nomadic Fulani whose Gerewol beauty contests also take place here.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Boule of millet with sauces, and grilled Nile perch from the lake and rivers.

culture.label: Languages
culture.text: Over 120 languages; French and Arabic are official and shared across a huge, thinly populated country.

talkAbout: The Ennedi and Zakouma National Park.
The rock art and the green Sahara.
The Toyota War, which Chadians recall with some pride.
avoid: The insurgency around Lake Chad, and Chad's long record of coups, are dangerous ground.

people.name: Barthélemy Boganda
people.why: A priest turned politician who designed the flag and died in a plane crash before independence.

people.name: Catherine Samba-Panza
people.why: Led the transitional government through the worst of the 2013–14 crisis.

people.name: Idylle Mamba
people.why: One of the country's best-known contemporary musicians.

people.name: Geoffroy Kondi
people.why: A guitarist working in the Central African Bantu and Sango popular traditions.

people.name: Karinou
people.why: Led the Kongo-Wara rebellion against French forced labour across a huge area.

events.title: The Kongo-Wara rebellion
events.what: A large revolt against French forced labour, suppressed and long left out of colonial histories.

events.title: Independence
events.what: The Central African Republic left French rule shortly after Boganda's death.

events.title: The empire
events.what: Bokassa crowned himself emperor in a coronation costing a large share of the national budget.

events.title: The crisis
events.what: Séléka and anti-balaka fighting displaced a quarter of the population.

culture.label: Pygmy polyphony
culture.text: The Aka people's overlapping vocal music is UNESCO-listed and has influenced composers worldwide.

culture.label: Dzanga-Sangha
culture.text: A forest clearing where hundreds of forest elephants gather at a mineral spring.

culture.label: Sango
culture.text: A creole that almost everyone speaks, alongside French — rare unity in a diverse country.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Cassava, plantain and bushmeat or river fish with groundnut sauce.

culture.label: Resources
culture.text: Diamonds, gold and timber, whose control has fuelled much of the conflict.

talkAbout: Sango, and how it holds the country together linguistically.
avoid: The ongoing conflict, foreign mercenaries and the Bokassa era are all difficult. One in five people is displaced.

people.name: Agostinho Neto
people.why: A doctor and poet who led the liberation movement and became the first president.

people.name: Queen Njinga
people.why: Fought the Portuguese for four decades through war and diplomacy, and is a national symbol.

people.name: Bonga
people.why: Sang semba in Kimbundu from exile and became Angola's most internationally known voice.

people.name: José Eduardo Agualusa
people.why: Won the International Dublin Literary Award and is Angola's leading contemporary writer.

people.name: Ana Paula Fernandes
people.why: Part of the generation raising Angola's profile in international basketball and handball.

events.title: Portuguese Angola
events.what: Nearly five centuries of colonial rule, and a major source of the transatlantic slave trade.

events.title: The war of independence
events.what: Guerrilla war against Portugal, which ended when Portugal's own dictatorship fell.

events.title: The civil war
events.what: Twenty-seven years of Cold War proxy conflict; the landmines are still being cleared.

events.title: Peace
events.what: Savimbi's death ended the war, and Angola began an oil-fuelled reconstruction boom.

culture.label: Kizomba & semba
culture.text: Semba is the older Angolan style; kizomba grew from it and is now danced worldwide.

culture.label: Capoeira's roots
culture.text: Engolo, an Angolan kicking game, is widely regarded as the ancestor of Brazilian capoeira.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Funge cassava dough with muamba de galinha, chicken in palm oil and okra.

culture.label: Languages
culture.text: Portuguese is dominant, with Umbundu, Kimbundu and Kikongo widely spoken.

culture.label: Landscape
culture.text: From the Namib desert in the south to rainforest in Cabinda, plus the Kalandula Falls.

talkAbout: Music and dance, especially kizomba's global spread.
avoid: The civil war and landmines are recent. Oil wealth, inequality and corruption cases are politically loaded.

people.name: Oliver Mtukudzi
people.why: Tuku music, and the country's most beloved musician across generations and politics.

people.name: Thomas Mapfumo
people.why: Created chimurenga music, adapting mbira songs into electric protest music.

people.name: Tsitsi Dangarembga
people.why: Nervous Conditions was the first novel in English by a Black Zimbabwean woman.

people.name: Kirsty Coventry
people.why: Seven Olympic medals — most of Zimbabwe's total — and now president of the IOC.

people.name: Nehanda Nyakasikana
people.why: Led resistance in the first Chimurenga and was hanged; her name became the movement's rallying cry.

events.title: Great Zimbabwe
events.what: A stone city built without mortar; colonial authorities long refused to credit Africans with it.

events.title: Rhodesia
events.what: A white minority regime declared independence unilaterally and fought a fifteen-year bush war.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Zimbabwe was born, with Robert Mugabe as prime minister and enormous international goodwill.

events.title: Hyperinflation
events.what: Prices doubled roughly every day; the hundred-trillion-dollar note is now a souvenir.

culture.label: Mbira
culture.text: The thumb piano is played to call ancestral spirits, and underpins much of Zimbabwean music.

culture.label: Stone sculpture
culture.text: Shona serpentine sculpture is collected worldwide and taught across generations of families.

culture.label: Victoria Falls
culture.text: Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders' — the largest sheet of falling water on earth.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Sadza with relish, and biltong; a braai is as much an institution as in South Africa.

culture.label: Literacy
culture.text: Among the highest literacy rates in Africa, sustained through decades of economic crisis.

talkAbout: Great Zimbabwe and the stone city.
Stone sculpture and the artists' communities.
avoid: Land reform, Mugabe's legacy and the Gukurahundi killings of the 1980s are all deeply divisive.

people.name: Seretse Khama
people.why: His marriage to a white Englishwoman caused an international crisis; he then led Botswana to independence.

people.name: Bessie Head
people.why: Wrote her major work in exile in Serowe; among southern Africa's most important writers.

people.name: Nijel Amos
people.why: Won Botswana's first Olympic medal, silver in the 800 m in 2012.

people.name: Unity Dow
people.why: Botswana's first woman High Court judge, and a novelist and campaigner.

people.name: Letsile Tebogo
people.why: Won the Olympic 200 m in 2024 — Botswana's first gold medal.

events.title: The Bechuanaland Protectorate
events.what: Three chiefs travelled to London to ask for British protection against the Boers and Rhodes.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Botswana became independent as one of the poorest countries on earth.

events.title: Diamonds at Orapa
events.what: The find that transformed the economy; the state negotiated an unusually good share of it.

events.title: Decriminalisation
events.what: The High Court struck down colonial-era laws criminalising same-sex relations.

culture.label: Wildlife
culture.text: The Okavango Delta floods into the Kalahari, and Botswana holds the largest elephant population on earth.

culture.label: Kgotla
culture.text: The village assembly where anyone may speak to the chief; consensus decision-making that still functions.

culture.label: Cattle
culture.text: Wealth and status are counted in cattle; the currency, the pula, means rain.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Seswaa — slow-pounded beef — with pap, and morogo wild greens.

culture.label: Baskets
culture.text: Botswana baskets, coiled from mokola palm with bark dyes, are museum pieces.

talkAbout: The kgotla and how decisions get made.
Athletics — Tebogo's 2024 gold was enormous here.
avoid: Relations with San/Basarwa communities and their removal from the Central Kalahari reserve are contested. HIV was a devastating epidemic here.

people.name: Sam Nujoma
people.why: Led SWAPO through the liberation war and became independent Namibia's first president.

people.name: Hendrik Witbooi
people.why: Fought German colonial forces and is on the banknotes as a national hero.

people.name: Frankie Fredericks
people.why: Four Olympic silver medals, and Namibia's most decorated athlete.

people.name: Christine Mboma
people.why: Won Olympic silver in the 200 m at eighteen.

people.name: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah
people.why: A liberation-era activist who became Namibia's first woman president in 2025.

events.title: The Herero and Nama genocide
events.what: German forces killed around 80% of the Herero and half the Nama; often called the first genocide of the 20th century.

events.title: South African rule
events.what: South Africa governed the territory and extended apartheid to it.

events.title: The liberation war
events.what: SWAPO's armed struggle, ending with a UN-supervised transition.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Namibia became independent, the last African country to escape colonial-style rule.

culture.label: Namib
culture.text: The world's oldest desert; the dunes at Sossusvlei are among the tallest anywhere.

culture.label: Conservancies
culture.text: Community conservancies cover a fifth of the country and brought black rhino back from the brink.

culture.label: Herero dress
culture.text: Herero women wear Victorian-style dresses with horn-shaped headwear, deliberately reclaiming an imposed costume.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Game meat, biltong, and German-derived sausage and bread from the colonial period.

culture.label: Dark skies
culture.text: The NamibRand reserve is one of the darkest places on earth for stargazing.

talkAbout: The desert and the Skeleton Coast.
Community conservancies, a genuine conservation success.
avoid: The genocide and Germany's slow acknowledgement of it are live issues. Land reform and inequality remain contested.

people.name: Samora Machel
people.why: Led FRELIMO to independence and became the first president; died in an unexplained plane crash.

people.name: Mia Couto
people.why: Reinvents Portuguese with Mozambican forms; winner of the Camões Prize.

people.name: Graça Machel
people.why: Education minister, UN expert on children in war, and the only woman to be first lady of two countries.

people.name: Maria Mutola
people.why: Olympic 800 m champion and Mozambique's only gold medallist.

people.name: Malangatana Ngwenya
people.why: Mozambique's best-known artist, whose murals cover public buildings across the country.

events.title: Portuguese Mozambique
events.what: Nearly five centuries of colonial rule along the Indian Ocean coast.

events.title: The independence war
events.what: FRELIMO's guerrilla campaign, ending when Portugal's dictatorship collapsed.

events.title: The civil war
events.what: Fifteen years of war backed by Rhodesia and South Africa killed around a million people.

events.title: Joining the Commonwealth
events.what: Mozambique joined despite never having been British — the first country to do so.

culture.label: Peri-peri
culture.text: The bird's eye chilli sauce is Mozambican; grilled prawns with it are the national dish.

culture.label: Marrabenta
culture.text: Guitar dance music from Maputo, built on Portuguese and local rhythms.

culture.label: Makonde carving
culture.text: Blackwood sculpture from the north, particularly the intertwined shetani and ujamaa figures.

culture.label: Ilha de Moçambique
culture.text: The old capital, a World Heritage island of coral-stone Portuguese and Swahili buildings.

culture.label: The flag
culture.text: Mozambique is the only country with a modern rifle on its flag, alongside a hoe and a book.

avoid: The civil war, and the insurgency in Cabo Delgado since 2017, are painful and current.

people.name: Kenneth Kaunda
people.why: Led Zambia to independence, governed for 27 years, and accepted defeat at the ballot box.

people.name: Dambisa Moyo
people.why: Dead Aid argued that aid harms Africa, and set off one of the field's fiercest arguments.

people.name: Kalusha Bwalya
people.why: African Footballer of the Year and the survivor who rebuilt the team after the 1993 crash.

people.name: Esther Phiri
people.why: A world champion who became one of Zambia's most recognisable sportspeople.

people.name: Namwali Serpell
people.why: The Old Drift won the Arthur C. Clarke Award and rewrote Zambia's history as fiction.

events.title: Victoria Falls
events.what: Livingstone became the first European to see Mosi-oa-Tunya, which the Kololo had long named.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Northern Rhodesia became Zambia under Kaunda.

events.title: The Gabon air disaster
events.what: The entire national football team died in a crash off Libreville; a new side reached the final a year later.

events.title: Africa Cup of Nations
events.what: Zambia won the final in Libreville, near where the 1993 team had died.

culture.label: Mosi-oa-Tunya
culture.text: Victoria Falls from the Zambian side, including the Devil's Pool at the very lip.

culture.label: Kuomboka
culture.text: The Lozi king's ceremonial move to higher ground when the Zambezi floods, in a great barge.

culture.label: Copperbelt
culture.text: Copper has driven the economy for a century, with all the booms and busts that implies.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Nshima with relish, kapenta dried fish, and village chicken.

culture.label: One Zambia
culture.text: 'One Zambia, One Nation' was Kaunda's slogan for holding 70-plus ethnic groups together, and it largely worked.

avoid: Debt and the cost of living are sore points. The 1993 crash is a national tragedy, not an anecdote.

people.name: Hastings Banda
people.why: A doctor in Britain for decades who returned to lead independence, then ruled for thirty years.

people.name: William Kamkwamba
people.why: Built a wind turbine from scrapyard parts at fourteen to power his family's home during a famine.

people.name: Joyce Banda
people.why: Malawi's first woman president, and only the second in Africa.

people.name: Lucius Banda
people.why: The Soldier of the Poor, whose reggae carried political criticism through the one-party years and after.

people.name: Legson Kayira
people.why: Walked around 4,000 km to Sudan hoping to reach America to study, and eventually got there.

events.title: Livingstone reaches the lake
events.what: He named it Lake Nyasa and campaigned against the slave trade running through the region.

events.title: The Chilembwe uprising
events.what: A pastor led a rising against colonial rule; his face is on the banknotes.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Nyasaland became Malawi under Banda.

events.title: Multiparty democracy
events.what: A referendum ended thirty years of one-party rule.

culture.label: Lake Malawi
culture.text: It holds more fish species than any other lake on earth, most found nowhere else.

culture.label: Warm Heart
culture.text: 'The warm heart of Africa' is the national nickname, and Malawians work at living up to it.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Nsima with relish, and chambo — the lake fish that is the national favourite.

culture.label: Gule Wamkulu
culture.text: The Chewa great dance, with masked figures representing spirits; UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Bicycle taxis
culture.text: Padded bicycle carriers are the standard local transport in much of the country.

talkAbout: Football, and how much the league means locally.
avoid: The Banda dictatorship and its detentions are still remembered. Poverty and aid dependence are frustrating subjects.

people.name: Ranavalona III
people.why: The last monarch of Madagascar, deposed and exiled by France in 1897.

people.name: Andrianampoinimerina
people.why: Unified the Merina kingdom and set Madagascar on the path to a single state.

people.name: Jean-Joseph Rabearivelo
people.why: Often called Africa's first modern poet; he wrote in French and Malagasy.

people.name: D'Gary
people.why: Adapted the valiha's techniques to guitar in tunings nobody else uses.

people.name: Michèle Rakotoson
people.why: One of Madagascar's leading writers, publishing across five decades.

events.title: Austronesian settlement
events.what: Madagascar was settled by seafarers from Borneo — 7,000 km away — which is why Malagasy is Austronesian.

events.title: The Merina kingdom
events.what: Radama I and Ranavalona I unified most of the island and resisted European control.

events.title: The Malagasy uprising
events.what: A revolt against French rule was crushed with tens of thousands of deaths.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Madagascar left French rule after sixty-five years.

culture.label: Endemism
culture.text: About 90% of Madagascar's wildlife exists nowhere else — every lemur species included.

culture.label: Famadihana
culture.text: The turning of the bones: families exhume ancestors, rewrap them in fresh shrouds and dance with them.

culture.label: Language
culture.text: Malagasy is Austronesian, closest to a language of Borneo, with Bantu and Arabic borrowings.

culture.label: Valiha
culture.text: A tube zither made from bamboo, the national instrument.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Rice at every meal — Malagasy eat more of it per head than almost anyone — with romazava stew.

talkAbout: The Austronesian origins, which surprise most people.
avoid: Famadihana is a sacred family rite, not a spectacle. Deforestation and vanilla-trade violence are difficult subjects.

people.name: Prince Louis Rwagasore
people.why: Won Burundi's first election and was assassinated two weeks later, aged 29.

people.name: Melchior Ndadaye
people.why: Burundi's first democratically elected Hutu president; his assassination triggered the civil war.

people.name: Khadja Nin
people.why: Burundi's best-known musician internationally, singing in Kirundi and Swahili.

people.name: Francine Niyonsaba
people.why: Olympic silver medallist over 800 m and a world record holder at 2,000 m.

people.name: Marguerite Barankitse
people.why: Saved and raised thousands of children orphaned by the war; the first Aurora Prize laureate.

events.title: The Kingdom of Burundi
events.what: A monarchy that lasted nearly three centuries through German and Belgian rule.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Burundi separated from Rwanda-Urundi and left Belgian administration.

events.title: The Ikiza
events.what: Mass killings of educated Hutu, with estimates from 80,000 to 200,000 dead.

events.title: The civil war
events.what: Twelve years of conflict ended by the Arusha accords and power-sharing.

culture.label: Royal drummers
culture.text: The Ingoma drummers of Gitega perform on hollowed trunks passed down through families; UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Landscape
culture.text: Hills throughout, with the southernmost source of the Nile and a shore on Lake Tanganyika.

culture.label: Coffee
culture.text: High-altitude arabica is the main export and increasingly prized by specialty roasters.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Beans and plantain, ugali, and mukeke fish from the lake.

culture.label: Kirundi
culture.text: Almost everyone speaks it — unusual in Africa — alongside French, English and Swahili.

avoid: The 1972 killings, the civil war and ethnic politics are extremely sensitive. Political discussion is risky.

people.name: Cesária Évora
people.why: The Barefoot Diva, who made morna a world music genre and won a Grammy at 62.

people.name: Amílcar Cabral
people.why: Led the liberation movement for both Cape Verde and Guinea-Bissau; one of Africa's foremost political thinkers.

people.name: Eugénio Tavares
people.why: Wrote in Creole when it was discouraged, and composed some of the best-loved mornas.

people.name: Germano Almeida
people.why: Won the Camões Prize, the highest honour in Portuguese-language literature.

people.name: Ryan Mendes
people.why: Long-serving captain of the Blue Sharks and the country's best-known player.

events.title: Settlement
events.what: Uninhabited before the Portuguese; Ribeira Grande became the first European town in the tropics.

events.title: The slave-trade entrepôt
events.what: The islands were a transshipment point, and Creole culture formed from that meeting.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Cape Verde became independent from Portugal after Cabral's movement's campaign.

events.title: Multiparty democracy
